title: Enforce expense bill and allocation authority independently of the MVC request pipeline
description: Stage 3 verified authorization-path gap, the same defect class already removed in ERP-462 / ERP-463 / ERP-464 / ERP-465 / ERP-466 / ERP-467 / ERP-468 / ERP-487 / ERP-492 / ERP-493. src/ERP.Api/Controllers/ExpenseBillController.cs:21 applies [ExpenseRequestAuthorizationFilter] as the only authority for every route, but that filter (src/ERP.Api/Controllers/BaseCrudController.cs:103-123, IAsyncActionFilter) runs only inside the MVC pipeline; each action instead reads ExpenseRequestScope (src/ERP.Api/Controllers/BaseCrudController.cs:31-35) which returns null whenever HttpContext.Items has no ExpenseRequestAuthorizationFilter.ScopeItemKey, and src/ERP.Application/Services/ExpenseAuthorizationRules.cs treats a null scope as unrestricted (ExpenseScopeFilter:259-263 and BatchScopeFilter:283-286 return no predicate, ApplyExpenseScope:268-274 returns the unfiltered source, EnsureBatchScopeAllowedAsync:384-390 and EnsureSettlementScopeAllowedAsync:424-430 return immediately), so an in-process call resolves no live identity, no ERP-453 account status, no existing expense-bill (费用单) menu and no ERP-097 customer scope for GetPaged:126, GetAll:136, GetById:146, Create:160, Update:177, Delete:213, BatchDelete:236, AllocatePreview:33, AllocateApply:46, GetAllocationContext:273, AllocationPreview:285, AllocationGenerate:297, GetAllocationBatches:307, GetAllocationBatch:316 and VoidAllocationBatch:328. Resolve the existing live authorization (ExpenseAuthorizationRules.EnsureMenuAuthorizedAsync:147) inside every action and use the returned non-null scope, remove the pipeline-shape waiver (filter application, ExpenseRequestScope property and the null-scope bypasses), and keep every existing boundary: persisted FinanceExpense.CustomerId ownership, shared-container participant / source-expense / per-line customer proof, allocation-basis freeze and void semantics, and zero writes on denial. Adapt the legacy in-process fixtures to genuine enabled identities holding their existing expense-bill grant in isolated test data only. No new menu, grant, permission, table or column, no anonymous, administrative, environment or test-only fallback, and no report or unrelated-module change. Safe Release build plus full ERP.UnitTests; genuine SQL only on the isolated localdb NEWERP_AutoAcceptance instance with a fresh GUID-owned NEWERP_AUTOTEST database. Preserve current business permissions and actor/customer scope; no new grants. Adapt all affected original fixtures with real enabled identities and existing menus/master rows, never remove business assertions or retain null-context/provider/test exceptions. Full original failure logs retained. Explicit test output/TRX/results directories must be .ai/logs/<task> only, never repository-root TestResults. SQL must use exactly (localdb)\NEWERP_AutoAcceptance with Integrated Security and a fresh GUID-owned NEWERP_AUTOTEST database; reject wrong/existing targets before access, never drop/reset. Safe Release restore/build with analyzers and warnings-as-errors, full units and relevant genuine isolated SQL validation; no whole-stage acceptance or production access.
acceptance_criteria: Every route on /api/finance/expenses (paged, all, by-id, create, update, delete, batch-delete, allocate-preview, allocate-apply, allocation-context, allocation-preview, allocation-generate, allocation-batches, allocation-batches/{batchId} and allocation-batches/{batchId}/void) resolves the current live enabled nondeleted identity, the ERP-453 account status and the existing expense-bill (费用单) menu through ExpenseAuthorizationRules.EnsureMenuAuthorizedAsync before any count, row, amount, allocation basis or write, independently of whether HttpContext is bound, whether Request.Path is set and whether the call passes through the MVC filter pipeline; the ExpenseRequestAuthorizationFilter application and the ExpenseRequestScope property are removed, missing/zero/unknown/deleted identity fails Unauthorized, disabled identity and missing/revoked menu fail Forbidden, and no anonymous, administrative, environment or test-only fallback is added.

Retain the existing expense and allocation boundaries and response contracts: authority is resolved live before any read, the resolved non-null scope is pushed down to SQL before count and paging, expense ownership stays the persisted FinanceExpense.CustomerId, allocation batches keep the explicit LoadingListId / SourceExpenseId / per-line customer proof, allocation-basis freeze and void semantics are unchanged, every denied route reads or writes zero FinanceExpenses, FinanceExpenseAllocationBatches and FinanceExpenseAllocationLines rows, and no new menu, grant, permission, table or column is added.

Adapt the legacy in-process expense fixtures to genuine enabled identities holding their existing expense-bill menu grants in isolated test data only, and add genuine unit plus isolated SQL controller tests covering every route for missing/zero/deleted identity, disabled and revoked-menu identity, limited-scope identity reading an out-of-scope expense or batch, no-HttpContext calls with empty and populated Request.Path, and permitted flows; existing ExpenseAuthorizationTests, ExpenseAllocationConcurrencyTests, ContainerExpenseAllocationTests, ContainerExpenseAllocationEvidenceTests and their SQL counterparts stay green.

Keep the safe Release build with analyzers and warnings-as-errors and the full existing ERP.UnitTests suite green, run genuine SQL only on the isolated localdb NEWERP_AutoAcceptance instance with Integrated Security and a fresh GUID-owned NEWERP_AUTOTEST database that is never dropped or reset, and claim no whole-stage acceptance from a build alone.
implementation_evidence: src/ERP.Api/Controllers/ExpenseBillController.cs:21 [ExpenseRequestAuthorizationFilter] is the class-level authority and lines 33/46/126/136/146/160/177/213/236/273/285/297/307/316/328 are the actions that instead read ExpenseRequestScope; src/ERP.Api/Controllers/BaseCrudController.cs:31-35 returns null unless HttpContext.Items contains ExpenseRequestAuthorizationFilter.ScopeItemKey and :103-123 show the filter is an IAsyncActionFilter that only executes inside the MVC pipeline; src/ERP.Application/Services/ExpenseAuthorizationRules.cs:259-263 ExpenseScopeFilter returns null for a null scope, :268-274 ApplyExpenseScope then returns the unfiltered source, :283-286 BatchScopeFilter likewise, :384-390 EnsureBatchScopeAllowedAsync and :424-430 EnsureSettlementScopeAllowedAsync return immediately for a null scope, while :147 EnsureMenuAuthorizedAsync is the existing live identity / account-status / expense-bill menu gate that the actions never call. src/ERP.UnitTests/ExpenseAuthorizationTests.cs:35-52 and :78-90 build controllers in-process and inject scope through HttpContext.Items, and src/ERP.IntegrationTests/ExpenseAuthorizationSqlServerTests.cs:60-63 does the same, which is exactly the fixture pattern that must be adapted; an exact search of .ai/tasks returns no task removing this filter waiver.
